name: Nishi-Eifuku
tagline: Shibuya in 17 minutes and Shinjuku in 20 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000.
summary: The station is in Suginami City, where Keio run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 41 minutes to Otemachi, 20 minutes to Shinjuku, 17 minutes to Shibuya and 43 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. The station stands 42.5 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 5.8 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 42.5 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 38.4 m to 44.2 m, a difference of 5.8 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 3 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 0.5 to 3 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 17 clinics and 13 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 樺島病院, about 5 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 樺島会樺島病院, about 5 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Keio Inokashira Line.
congestion: Keio Inokashira Line runs at 125% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 池ノ上→駒場東大前, which this station is not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥70,000 to ¥80,000 and 1K ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. 1LDK ¥150,000 to ¥160,000 and 2LDK ¥210,000 to ¥220,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

neighbours.lead: Hamadayama is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection and how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Nishi-Eifuku. It is served by the same lines as Nishi-Eifuku. Journey times to the main business districts are much the same. On how easy the shopping is, Hamadayama comes out ahead.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 3 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 4 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Keio Inokashira Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
